title: Key invariant: the pair of longest increasing/decreasing sequence lengths for Erdős–Szekeres
intent: Prove the Erdős–Szekeres theorem — more than r*s distinct values force an increasing sequence longer than r or a decreasing sequence longer than s — by labelling each index i with the pair of longest increasing and decreasing sequence lengths ending at i, proving that labelling injective, and pigeonholing more than r*s elements into the r×s box of possible labels.

parent.name: erdos_szekeres
parent.statement:
theorem erdos_szekeres {r s : ℕ} {f : α → β} (hn : r * s < Fintype.card α) (hf : Injective f) :
    (∃ t : Finset α, r < #t ∧ StrictMonoOn f t) ∨
      ∃ t : Finset α, s < #t ∧ StrictAntiOn f t

applicability.goal_shape: A pigeonhole argument over a finite type: prove that if a structure is large enough, some object of a given kind must exist. The move attaches to each element a canonical pair (here the maximum length of an increasing and of a decreasing sequence ending there), shows the labelling is injective, and bounds the set of possible labels by the size of the counter-assumption.
applicability.use_when: the existence of a long monotone (or otherwise extremal) subsequence can be re-phrased as 'some element has a large label'; the invariant's injectivity is a short case split (here on i < j vs j < i); and the label set is a product of two finite intervals so its size is a product.
applicability.avoid_when: the invariant cannot be made injective (the two label components need separate comparison lemmas); the label set is not a clean finite product (so the cardinality bound is not r*s); or the extremal object is not 'attained' by a maximum over a nonempty finite set (here supplied by max'_mem and the singleton one_mem lemmas).

claims.claim: The authors state the invariant and the pigeonhole plan in the theorem's docstring: "We label each value in the sequence with two numbers specifying the longest increasing subsequence ending there, and the longest decreasing subsequence ending there. We then show the pair of labels must be unique. Now if there is no increasing sequence longer than r and no decreasing sequence longer than s, then there are at most r * s possible labels, which is a contradiction if there are more than r * s elements."

consequences: The move obliges the writer to (i) prove the invariant is attained at every index (maxIncSequencesTo_mem / maxDecSequencesTo_mem, from the nonemptiness of the singleton sequence), (ii) prove the invariant is injective, which is a two-way case split on i < j vs j < i backed by the two comparison lemmas maxIncSequencesTo_lt and maxDecSequencesTo_gt, and (iii) bound the label set below by 1 (one_le_maxIncSequencesTo / one_le_maxDecSequencesTo) so it is exactly the product box Icc 1 r ×ˢ Icc 1 s. Failure mode: the injectivity rests on order duality — maxDecSequencesTo_gt is maxIncSequencesTo_lt on βᵒᵈ — so the invariant only works when both the increasing and decreasing halves are stated with the same 'ends at i' notion; if the extremal object were a supremum that need not be attained, the one_mem / max'_mem lemmas would not exist and the argument would need a different completion.
